tips.comment: The model I run suggests The Lion In Winter can win this race. The Lion In Winter has by far the highest RPR of the 11 runners here, but isn't penalized in the weights at all. All runners go out carrying the same amount. No jockeys are claiming or have anything else to be factored into the weights equation. 267 days since last run is a serious gap, so may lack some race fitness, but form before that was all wins. If anywhere back to that form when coming out fresh, should go close.

Here makes the appearance of the current Derby favourite, the unbeaten Aidan O'Brien trained The Lion In Winter, winner of the Acomb Stakes here last August. The Charlie Appleby/Godolphin team had the third home that day, Ruling Court, currently 3rd favourite for the Epsom classic, although not exactly buzzy. If there's going to be a lowering of the Coolmore star's colours, I think it will come from the same team who have the aforementioned Ruling Court, the unbeaten Alpine Trail. Easy winner of the Newmarket Stakes at the Guineas meeting and supplemented for 14,000 gns on Friday for this, he looks a strong each way bet.

Wimbledon Hawkeye was 2nd to The Lion In Winter as a two year old here at York and has the benefit of two runs so far this season in the Craven Stakes and 2000 Guineas at Newmarket in which he hung right in the latter stages of both. He looks good for at least a place here at York and could get closer to the favourite with race fitness.

Disappointed to miss the early 25-1, but 16-1 is fair enough. The last 4f on the clock at Sandown were very fast over the wrong trip and will come on a bundle for that run. Really excited about this horse and don't think Lion in Winter will be all out to win.

Lingfield novice winner who reappeared with a mighty effort to land the listed Blue Riband Trial at Epsom at 40/1. That's amongst the best form on offer here so would be no surprise to see this son of Sea The Stars run very well at a price.

The only win last season for See The Fire came here at York over nine furlongs in a Group 3 race but her other six runs were all at Group 1 level and she failed by only a neck when 2nd to Opera Singer in the Nassau Stakes at Goodwood. She was a beaten favourite first time out at Sandown in a Group 3 when only 5th of 7 but only beaten two lengths and that should have brought her on.

The 4yo filly spent last year running to a decent level overseas in good races. Decent UK run on her return at the start of this month when 3rd in a Group 2 race, up against Group 1 capable runners. Can improve for the run in this Group 2 contest. William Buick in the saddle and no problem with the quick ground.
Looks sure to run a big race. He looks the EW steal, but I just feel See The Fire is a bit better. She is regally bred.

Won Fresh last year and this horse is a really gritty one. I don't think this race is deep at all and expect Royal Dress to be delivered late. She will be wound up fully for this and I'm confident she can get up near the line.

The model I run suggests each way on Sioux Life is the value play here. Sioux Life has had quite a large gap of 200 days between the last run and this one, but before that was showing some exceptional form with 4 wins from 5. If anywhere near that form, it could come close here over the 1m 2f distance. Plumb draw in stall one helps, giving the opportunity to run the rail and cover less distance if preferred tactics.

Race fitness would probably be the main concern here. However, it was a nice horse last season, winning 4 out of 7 and ran a nice race, finishing 6th in the Breeders' Cup Juvenile despite dwelling at the start and running keen throughout before being short of room in the last furlong. Form ties in closely with Big Mojo, who's since come out and won and is undoubtedly the best horse in this if turning up.

Tropical Storm finished 4th behind Aesterius in a Group 2 at Doncaster in September but had previously run well when winning a Listed race here at York on good to firm. In receipt of five pounds from the favourite, he might turn the tables.

The 3yo filly has 3 wins from 5 and is still unexposed. A big run on the AW two weeks ago after a 7-month break, drawn widest, raced wide, and slightly hampered turning into the straight, losing out in the last strides in a decent Listed contest. Plenty of room for improvement. Ryan Moore in the saddle. No problem with the quick turf ground in this Listed contest.

Sir Yoshi ran a very credible 3rd at this course and distance last season, and could be suited by a forecasted fast pace once again. He's run his best races on fast ground, which he will be getting here once again.

American Affair won very easily on reappearance, and has only gone up 4 pounds for that. I'm expecting the pace to collapse here, as there is so much pace. This horse will be in the perfect position to take advantage of this. I'm not sure if stall 16 is good here, but it looks like there's pace everywhere.

Shagraan has to shoulder top weight here, but he was really progressive as a 3-year-old last season, winning twice and placing (including extra places) a further four times in competitive handicaps. That saw his mark rise to 101, which was the same as his reappearance third when just 0.5L back on seasonal return and just 3lbs higher than when fifth here at the Ebor meeting on his only visit to York. He was the only one of the top six to race off the pace that day, meaning it can be massively upgraded. There's so much pace on offer here that there's the potential for a real burn-up, and his likely hold-up tactics can bear fruit. Now a 4-year-old, I think he can show himself to be a pattern performer at sprinting trips.

The 4yo was a winner of a 28-runner handicap at Royal Ascot last year on fast ground. Big Return ran three weeks ago, after a 6-month break, beaten under a length in a decent handicap - posting a big RPR rating. Room for improvement after that run.

This is wide open with plenty of possibilities, but I'm keen on ZOULU CHIEF, who had been off the track during 2024 before showing he had retained ability when third at Ascot. He had won at the Ebor meeting in 2023 off 1lb higher. If running to that standard again, it would be a very positive each-way bet with 5 places on offer with most bookies.

The model I run suggests Fine Wine is the value bet here and could cause a surprise. This result has largely been driven by Fine Wine having the joint highest RPR of the field and the second lowest official ranking. This means Fine Wine lines up with the least amount of weight to carry in this large 18-horse race. Aiden Brookes is one of the few claiming jockeys on the card and is picking up the reins of Fine Wine. He relieves 3 lbs of weight with his claim. The stall draw of 17 is really not helpful but looks more than baked into the price at 21s. A good 3rd 13 days ago and is a prior course and distance winner here at York over 5f.

The best form of Toca Madera has been on good to firm and firm going and he should be suited by conditions at York and should be in the first five home with Tommie Jakes taking off five pounds allowance.

Mondammej knows this track very well but has surprisingly never won a race here. He's a horse which comes off the pace, which is the profile I'm looking for here. He's down to a mark of 80 and showed promise on the All-Weather. Place shout at these odds.

FRIO is the rightful fav here and 7/4 should be taken. Utmost Respect carries a dreadful FlatStats rating alongside M Scaife's 3% SR (A/E 0.32) at Northern courses, meanwhile Ballistic Missile's barely comes out better on FS ratings and S Foley does pretty awful over in the UK (6% SR, A/E 0.6). I couldn't make a case for the remainder so the jolly should win by default as well as on merit. The son of Havana Grey made a promising debut at Musselburgh last month; losing 3l to C2 performing Dickensian and NTO winner Clear Force after being squeezed up at the start. He carries a lofty top + blue FlatStats rating alongside HG's impressive 53% SR (A/E 1.33) with favourites in May boosting claims.
The stable does well with two-year-old newcomers this year, and this one looks well worth interest on debut. Well-bred and will have been well-schooled.

The selection is making his debut in this average looking 6 runner novice stakes. The trainer has good career stats with his 2yo runners, sending out plenty of quality youngsters in recent years. You would expect he’d be using one of his better types with a first prize of £20K in this contest.

Bravo Hotel shaped better than the bare result on debut, slowly into stride but staying on late. Likely to improve for the run and could find this stiff 5f more to his liking. At 16/1, he's a value each-way play in a race full of unexposed types. A better break could see him grab a place or more.

Drawn with the pace but unlikely to be too close and should be able to sit off. Winner and placed at this level, including win off 94 and 0.5L 3rd off 99. Decent season last season despite only winning one, had plenty of good runs in decent handicaps. Two good runs this season when keeping on well for 2nd over 1m and being beat 0.5L 2nd at Chester from stall 12, having sweated up and raced wide. Should be hitting peak fitness now and Easterby going to 18% SR. Plenty of pace from Thunder Run, Salamanca, and a couple others, and unlikely they'll be able to sustain it here over a CD where the bias heavily favors horses mid-held up. Also has strength advantage over the 4yos as they won't have matured fully until around August.

Zain Blue has saved his best for York, finishing 2nd behind Battle Cry in his maiden (that rival a Group 3 winner since), then 5th and 1st in two handicaps over C&D, winning from a mark of 83 in first-time cheekpieces. Headgear left off for his reappearance but now goes back on and he's just 2 lbs higher than his win here in September. Up in grade but looks fairly weighted and well drawn (stall 8) with Thunder Run going forward from stall 4. Yard are in decent form having had a few winners in the last couple of weeks.
Merchant was staying on over ten furlongs at Newmarket first time out this season. He should be suited by the extra distance and fast going at York and is two pounds well in with the handicapper.

The model I run suggests Many Men can win this one. This result has largely been driven by Many Men having the second highest RPR of the field, but the second lowest OR. This leaves him carrying the second lowest weight over this 1m 3f trip. Jack Doughty on board claims a further 3 lbs, which is helpful. Stall 6 draw isn't the best, but very manageable over the longer distance.
Penn Avenue for the Kublers looks to be the one to back here, has the highest rating in the field and looked to have a good return to racing last time.

BUCK BARROW had a sire who did well over this distance and this one makes his stable debut with the yard in form often doing particularly well at this venue. That bodes well for the placement of this young horse racing in a low level handicap and he could get involved.

BATTLE STRIDE looks very interesting in this race. Michael Bell has a decent strike rate at Bath and a super 30% SR in the last fortnight. This horse is untested on fast ground, but Michael is an experienced trainer and wouldn't run him if it wasn't suitable for him. This horse is a massive player.

Ottoman is a lot more interesting than the form book on paper is suggesting returned to action on the 7th of April 2025 after a 161 day break having exchanged hands and joined a new stable in the process of that break now after 2 runs for his new yard he arrives here in a much fitter state and is better adjusted back home at his new yard steps up in trip going over 1 mile 2 furlongs for the first time that being a good move by his connections as this new trip can unlock a whole new level of improvement currently operating on a very dangerous mark of 54 O Greenall & J Guerriero's new recruit looks poised to trouble the judge on this outing jockey Aiden Brookes takes off a handy 3lb which only enhances his good looking claims here in what is a suitable assignment for this individual likely to be a whole different proposition this time out especially over this new trip gelded son of Acclamation & Kaftan ( Dam's sire Dansili ) must be taken very seriously of this sort of mark and shouldn't be by any means underestimated

Has been in decent form on the AW, winning a class 6 over 8.5f and didn't fare too badly last time out when only beaten 2L in a class 6 at Lingfield on its first try over 10f. Has something to prove on its return to turf but is down from a class 4 maiden on the surface to class 6 handicap today. Is top-rated in some quarters and has a decent course jockey booked. Trainer and jockey's only runner of the day.

This horse is friendless at 50/1 in the early market and comes with the proviso that she'd only really be of interest if there was any market support since this is a gambling stable. Reasons for thinking we might see a marked improvement, though, are the first-time cheekpieces and the first-time booking of Jason Watson on the horse. His strength in the saddle looks exactly what is required since the horse hasn't been straightforward for weaker jockeys. The step up in trip will also suit and help the horse settle, and progeny of the sire do really well on firm ground, which often occurs at Bath and doesn't suit many horses. In fact, the sire's progeny have a record over c&d on firm ground of 11353020, which is 2 wins and 3 places from just 8 runs, which suggests the 50/1 might be worth taking.

Baileys Value lines up in the 20:12 at Bath tomorrow, the Blackmore Building and Design Handicap??'a Class 6 contest over 1 mile 2 furlongs and 37 yards. Trained by Lemos Souza, this 3-year-old filly by Bated Breath has shown gradual improvement in her recent outings. 
After a series of unplaced efforts, she stepped up to 1m1f at Wolverhampton in March, finishing a respectable third at 66/1. Her latest run at Brighton over 1m2f saw her finish sixth of nine, suggesting she's finding her stride over these longer distances. 
Returning to turf on Bath's firm ground could play to her strengths. With George Wood taking the ride, Baileys Value presents a compelling each-way proposition in this field.

A touch disappointing on his return to action this season, hammered off the boards at Windsor but was only able to plug on at one pace for third. This stiffer finish could be a help to him and he is entitled to sharpen up for the run.
On a bit of a winning run at the moment, and although I tend to steer clear of horses on sequences, I can't get past I Follow Rivers here.

At the bottom of the handicap mark in this field, but at least gained valuable experience over C&D last September. Now makes handicap debut tomorrow, and if improvements are made, then I think he has a chance, which is helped by dropping down in class.
No comment made
There has been money for this Andrew Balding horse on both starts to date, but it has yet to trouble the judge. Again, there has been interest, so there might be improvement to come.
MEHMAS AIR FORCE, fifth on her racecourse debut over 5f at Leicester last month, should have come on for that run. Upped in trip to 6f should suit and could well be able to win this race.

Race 2 at Bath today is a Maiden (Class 4) for 2-year-olds over 1,152 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 2-year-old gelding Eightthreeone from the Eve Johnson Houghton yard, and will be ridden by Georgia Dobie. This son of Rumble Inthejungle had a decent debut at this course when a good 2nd earlier this month. He should improve on that showing and is one to consider.

SQUADRON LEADER by a great sprinter in Mehmas. He won over slightly further (6f) at Group 1 level, so can easily get involved here. I know the market says Richard Hughes's runner should win, BUT when I checked Flatstats, I didn't find the results supported that theory. Archie Watson's record is definitely more convincing, and that's why I will be backing this horse each way.

TOUCHWOODNWHISTLE was green on his debut , but this juvenile with his noteworthy sprint sire could be a big improver second time up. Professional jockey ridden today and with no obvious big gap to bridge on RPR from this line-up he appeals.
Malinga The Slinga, eleventh on his racecourse debut over 5f at Beverley last month, should have come on for that run. Upped in trip to 6f should suit and could well be able to win this race.
A winner when last seen at this venue. She was strong at the finish that day, suggesting this longer trip is well within range. She has a 5lb penalty, but that looks fair. She has a big chance.

A small field with in-form runners here, but Darysina Gold is the pick to win. Darysina Gold is a course winner, and market confidence last time was good. However, she pulled too hard and could not settle. If she relaxes early on, she can be the dark horse in this race.

Needed the run at Kempton last time after a break and should be fitter for this much poorer race. Hasn't won yet but the form of the Kempton third in the Autumn would give him a real chance tonight. Drops another three pounds and now thirteen below the high mark. This is the second run back after wind surgery which can be a positive.

Jimmy Mark thrives at Bath, with three career wins at the course and a recent victory over this trip. He’s well-suited to firm ground and front-running tactics, making him dangerous if allowed to dictate. The Kittow-Hornby pairing adds further confidence. A genuine contender with conditions in his favor.

Blue Hero returns to a track he likes and runs off a mark close to his last winning one. He was a solid third over course and distance last time out and should be competitive again if fit and ready after a break.

Up 4 pounds from the last win but Two Plus Two can make it a double in this low grade open handicap. Won nicely at Salisbury 10 days ago and remains very well-treated under a penalty. Proven at the trip and adaptable on firm ground. If he handles the quick turnaround, he's very hard to oppose in this grade.

HAWK JET may have found a suitably soft looking middle-distance handicap where she can make his mark and break her maiden. She has the considerable assistance of Sean Dylan Bowen in the saddle tonight nand given the red-hot form of the yard her lack of a recent ru in this low grade may not be an issue.

We can safely put a line through this selection's latest effort when its jockey and the one aboard another of tonight's rivals, Two Plus Two, lost their minds and went off at a suicidal pace. Two Plus Two has subsequently won, which is a positive. If we take a moment to look back at the nap's previous run, you will see a true measure of the ability that will hopefully be revealed here back on turf, as it was full of running on the penultimate run but all the doors kept closing. Confident nap selection - get on!
Unseated over hurdles last time. Possibly didn't stay on penultimate start when going for the HT. Worth an each-way bet back down in trip.

Endofastorm lines up in the 19:42 at Bath tomorrow, the Best Odds Guaranteed At Yeeehaaa.Bet Handicap??'a Class 6 contest over 1 mile 3½ furlongs for three-year-olds. Trained by Joe Ponting, this 6-year-old mare by Galileo Gold has shown a consistent profile, with 3 wins and 4 placings from 27 career starts. 
Her recent form includes a third-place finish at Wolverhampton on 6 May 2025 in a Class 5 handicap over 1m5f219y, where she was beaten by just over 11 lengths. Prior to that, she secured a victory at Wolverhampton on 9 December 2024 in a Class 6 race over 1m4f51y on the all-weather surface. 
The expected firm ground at Bath should suit her, given her previous successes on similar surfaces. With her proven ability over the distance and under these conditions, Endofastorm presents a compelling each-way proposition in this field.

Uther Pendragon is a veteran who has won four times on the flat, with twenty placed efforts. The last of those wins was a course and distance win, off a higher handicap mark than he runs off today. Each way chance.

Takeonedayatatime has the best form in the field. The ground should suit. Finished 3rd of 8 last time out and was beaten by 5 lengths on debut at Wincanton on good ground. Has the strongest claims and is hard to oppose.

FALSE FLAG runs for a powerful NH yard and this filly may have found a suitable opening for her career debut. Her dam was a Bumper winner and there is the stamina in her family to think she is the right type to land a race of this nature.

The model I run suggests Robin Blue Breast could win this one. Robin Blue Breast steps out with the highest RPR of the field, and all runners here go out carrying the same weight. Takeonedayatatime is the current very short-priced market favorite, but that does not represent value here. Next best looks like Robin Blue Breast. Callum Pritchard is a trusted jockey on board and relieves a further 5 lbs off the total weight, which does give a competitive advantage over the 2m trip.

Poor bumper race and worth a poke going each way with Musique Des Champs. Ran in a low-grade conditions race, finishing fourth. Now goes under rules for Kailey Woolacott, who does okay with her bumper runners. Still a filly, and she's by Jukebox Jury. The sire does well on good ground.

Happy Index won over 2m4f here in September and again at Market Rasen in November. He returned from a break when 3rd here over 3 miles last month. He should appreciate the step up to 3m2f on quicker ground, and with Sean Bowen booked to ride, he looks the most likely winner here.
The in-form Candlish yard is going well, and this gelding is improving. Sean Quinlan is amongst the winners too, and the extra distance could mean more improvement.

Artic Mann has been running in Class 4 handicaps for the last year or so, unlike his rivals who have been going in Class 5 races mostly. His run in April over CD was a good effort in a better race than this, and he is unlikely to be inconvenienced by the quicker ground here. He won this race last year and looks sure to go well again.

Assuming Schmilsson can jump the larger obstacles he can win this very ordinary Novice Handicap Chase. His hurdle form is well in advance of these, and the top weight is one who I can always readily avoid as he isn't the most resolute of animals.
Yet to win over fences, but this looks like a good chance. Was a very good 2nd last time out after absence. Should be fitter for that, and this course and distance suits.

Disco Annie has been given two tough assignments in the last four runs. She has been running between hurdles and chasing. Two wins in good fashion at Carlisle and runner-up efforts at the same venue and Cartmel. She should enjoy good ground conditions and is unexposed on her third chase start. She should threaten back in this company.

Third in a five-runner Ayr maiden last time out, with Green Sky being taken out of the race. It looks almost inconceivable that this race won't be taken. Perfect opportunity to get a win on the board.
More than a year since his last win, but his mark has been steadily dropping and has now reached a level where he can be competitive, carrying only 1 lb more than on his last victory.

Should have put this up last night when I picked it out and it was double the price! I've said before about liking these apprentice and conditional jockey races as there can be some great value in jockeys who are able to claim significant weight over jockeys with not much more experience or ability. Prime example here where Joshua Thompson can claim 6lb over other conditionals. Compare this to a regular handicap where he would claim 7lb over professional and vastly more experienced jockeys. He has 12 wins to his name and though a strike rate of 7% is a little low, he does ride a lot of big-priced outsiders with little chance. Currently riding with plenty of confidence, he has a recent win to his name while also boasting 5 top 3 finishes in the last 14 days. The horse has yet to win but is lightly raced, shaped with promise last time, and should benefit from stepping back up in trip.

Maillot Blanc is on a long losing streak, and the visor needs to spark improvement today. A half-decent 6th last time out, so I am expecting at the very minimum a place here, as a huge jockey claimer of 10 pounds could be a massive help here.
Hasn't done much lately but had a good spell last year with back-to-back wins, including one here at Perth, and not much else standing out.
First time in a handicap may be the right time to catch this ex-Irish mare. The yard is going very well and has patiently brought her along.
Somptueux has won two of his three points this spring, likes a sound surface, and has Gina Andrews on board. So his long trip north to Perth should be a winning one.
Colonel Whizz, it's his chase debut and needs to bounce back from the last run. Olly Murphy is in excellent form, and the yard is flying. Sean Bowen is an excellent booking.
First run for a new yard but has been remarkably consistent at Perth before without a win. Finished in the top four in all five starts, placing three times here.

This race looks pretty desperate and I am convinced that Wotsmyname could finally shed his maiden tag. He's travelled a lot sweeter since being fitted with cheekpieces and I believe the eight-year-old has every chance off a 9lb lower mark than his latest fourth at Kelso, where he only gave way on the run-in.

The yard seemed to have found the key to Larkfield Lusive last time. He joined just over a year ago and, following racing over various trips and ground, went as close as he's been a month ago. Still only 6 years old, and connections will get more from him yet. This race looks like a winning opportunity.

Hasn't been the most consistent in his career, but Rickety Gate seemed to enjoy a fair drop in trip. Normally campaigned at 3m to 2m3f and won with 2 lengths to spare. That was in class 4 company and races back at this trip and same ground conditions but dropping into class 5 company. Should have too much for rivals. NAP

MILLYUPDAHILLY drops considerably in class following a fair effort in a much deeper handicap latest. She is race-sharp with potential to be seen to much better effect in this company , and not yet fully exposed under this code in Britain with this trainer having recorded multiple wins at this venue she should be heavily involved.

BEAT THE RETREAT has won two hurdle races at 2m 2f and 2m 4f. Fifth in a hurdle race over 3m at Perth on his latest outing last month. Dropped in trip to 2m 4f should suit. Seems well treated and could well be able to win this race.

Not sure why they have been so disappointing on last 4 runs, as they were in decent form @ the end of last year and into 2025. However, is a C/D winner with a 33 percent course profile, so coming back here a big plus, good conditional up taking off 3lb and shrewd trainer is 24 percent with a Lsp of 23.00 on her hurdlers here last 5 seasons, making current 10/1 very good Ew value in the race.
Back from a break having last run in mid December. Vastly experienced, has won four times here at Perth, and conditions could be good here.

The model I run suggests Gonnino can win this one. This result has been driven by Gonnino lining up with the second highest PRR of the group. All 11 runners line up carrying the same weight. Last ran 38 days ago, so racing fitness shouldn't be an issue. Gary Rutherford has a high RTF%.

The horse won on its only other previous visit to the course in September 2024 in Class 4 on good, off a mark of 114. It also won on the last run over today's 24f trip at Ffos Las in Class 4 on good to soft, off a mark of 116. That win came 28 days ago, and the horse is upped a further 5lb. Team Bowen won this race last year with the top weight and aren't making the 854-mile round trip for a day out.

The model I run suggests Everyday Champagne is the value bet here. Everyday Champagne lines up with the second highest RPR of the runners but has the lowest official ranking. This leaves him carrying the lowest weight in the race by some distance. The next lowest weight being carried is 10 lbs more, and the market leading horse is carrying the heaviest amount, it's a weight differential of 21 lbs, which is significant over what is essentially a 3m round trip.

The model I run suggests Cuban Cigar could cause an upset here and is the value play. Cuban Cigar lines up in this 7-horse race with by far the highest RPR, but the lowest OR. This subsequently leaves him carrying the lowest weight of the 7 runners. He is a previous distance winner over this 2m trip and has Alan Doyle on board claiming a further 5 lbs off his back.

My vote here goes to Off The Bench who's turn to strike is near in very good time was last seen at Bath 15 day's ago where finishing a never nearer 4th/8 now he did shape with plenty of promise and he really is starting to get the hang of things however the drop in trip to 5 furlongs on that occasion wasn't ideal and 6 furlongs looks to be the best option distance wise and that is the distance he will be racing over here today and is likely to be shown in much better light here over a more suitable trip is now lurking on an extremely dangerous mark of 56 and this gelded son of Ardad & Davinci Dawn ( Dam's sire Poet's Voice ) looks poised to strike of this sort of mark especially having found a suitable looking race to fit into here jockey Finley Marsh takes the ride on J S Moore's inmate and he must enter calculations in a race of this nature

The model I run suggests 'She Is For Me Boys' should win this one. Lines up with by far the highest RPR of the field and steps out carrying similar weight to most of the other horses running. Top of the market, 'The Secret Pearl' carries an extra 7 lbs and could be telling over the 2m 1f trip.

The model I run suggests Sambezi should win this race. This model result has been driven by Sambezi having by far the highest RPR of the field and a kind official ranking. This leaves him carrying only effectively the second lowest weight of the 8-runner field. Sambezi is a previous course and distance winner, last ran 25 days ago, meaning race fitness shouldn't be an issue. Also has the highest top speed by quite a margin.

The model I run suggests an upset here for Ultra Viers. This simulated result has largely been driven by Ultra Viers having the highest RPR of the field, and a fairly low official ranking compared to the other 7 runners. This leaves him running on a very workable mark and goes out carrying 1 stone and a half less than the current market favourite. Last ran 20 days ago. Needs to show some improvement after going 4,4,4 but open to doing that off this mark.

The model I run has simulated this race and suggests Rockola should win this one. Rockola lines up with the second highest RPR of the field but has the lowest official ranking of the 7 runners. This leaves him carrying the lowest weight of the runners over this 2m 5f round trip.

the model I run suggests Hatos could cause a bit of an upset here. Others more prominent in the early market but this looks like the value play. Hatos has by far the highest RPR of the 5 runners here. Does go out carrying a stone more than the others over the 2m race. Joe Tizard has a high RTF %. Didn't look too out of place when last running in a class 2 handicap 48 days ago, now drops back to a class 5 handicap chase and could cause an upset.

The model I run suggests Hard Stare can win this one. This model result has been driven by Hard Stare having by far the highest RPR of the lineup. No official ranking data to go by, but all horses are carrying weights within a fairly tight banding. None of the jockeys on board are claiming, so this represents a true picture of the weight distribution. Hard Stare wears a tongue tie for the first time to aid concentration.

Gelded son of Kodiac & Invitational ( Dam's sire Poet's Voice ) who has been brought along steadily makes his seasonal reappearance and handicap debut here after a 214 day break having also been gelded in the process of that break and strongly appeals as the type to do much better now heading down the handicap route begins life in handicaps of a very attractive mark of 65 and Rogar Varian's inmate is likely to be much better than that in very good time now heading down the handicap route this looks a perfect starting point in handicaps and Kosometsuke is of serious interest here jockey J Mitchell takes the ride and can give Kosometsuke a promising ride here at Kempton . Respected .

Sunny South West won on rules debut in a bumper at Clonmel in March and then ran well to finish 5th in a Grade 1 at Punchestown when 66/1. This is much calmer waters, and if he runs to the same level, he should be winning here.

Moon Eclipse won nicely first time out for Joseph O'Brien beating the second horse who went on to run well in a Grade 2 at Aintree and the third who looks a very nice horse and went on to run very well at Fairyhouse next time for Willie Mullins. Things didn't work out next time in a very hot listed race but she can return to form in this easier contest.

ANGELO DUNDEE is often well punted and some of his placed form in Bumpers reads even better than his career debut win. He has a promising 7lb claiming cionditional jockey aboard and he rares the value play with his fitness worth chancing.
Won well at Galway last time out and is in with a real chance here as long as overcoming the nine and a half months' break.

GIMME A BUZZ given time represents a high-profile yard and surely has something to spare from his lowly handicap mark. He is ridden by Mark Walsh on behalf of J P McManus and this is a weak handicap where he should be capable of landing a blow.
I can't look beyond the market leader in this race as Patty O'Farrell, who has been steadily improving recently and should improve further from a good 2nd place last time out.

Lightly raced sort, back down in trip for his handicap hurdle debut. Makes said debut off a lowly weight. Jockey in decent form. Trainer's last couple have performed well. Looks set to improve and could go well tonight.

Is a much better horse on good ground as they showed 5/6 runs back, so going is coming in their favour and is very nicely handicapped here off dropping mark of 83, so current 14/1 would represent decent Ew value here.

5 places and bigger odds, Fourcardrun can be a dark horse today as improvement seems likely. On a mark of 90 and a 3 pound claimer taking it to 87 he is very well handicapped here. Fourcardrun has had 3 quiet novice runs and was not knocked around like some. He enters my calculations in handicaps now and could step forward off a bargain basement mark. He is a big runner at a very good price here.
Not one of the most consistent of runners, but a recent win at Gowan Park reads really well. If coming here in that sort of form, it gives this one a big chance.

As always, I’m looking for a bigger price, and one that interests me is Fran Flood’s 7-year-old mare SPANISH MAID. This charge posted some solid efforts in maiden hurdle company, most notably a 3rd (beaten 2 lengths) here at Tipperary last May. That was followed by a 3rd & 4th at Sligo and 5th at Fairyhouse. This daughter of WORKFORCE was then sent over fences, taking on the likes of Zenta, Paggane, and Springt De La Mare - all of whom have progressed nicely since.
The return to hurdles looks the right move. Despite her bloodline, her best run came here at Tipperary on yielding ground. Nearly all of her other runs (bar one) were on testing ground, so it’s interesting to see how she fares today on the current good/ yielding surface. Donagh Meyler retains the ride and has a respectable 20.97% place strike rate at Tipperary over the past five years. Trainer Fran Flood hasn’t had a winner since 2022, but a return to the scene of his mares best performance offers some hope. At current odds of 25/1 with 5 places on offer, I wouldn’t be putting the mortgage on her. but hitting the frame certainly isn’t impossible.
Ran a good 3rd in December but has not shown much in the last couple of runs. Dropped down the weights today, gets its favoured ground, and will make a bold show today.

Backward type who has had only 3 runs under rules, despite being 5 years old. Won his bumper last November despite being green, and greenness let him down in follow-up bid in December. Made hurdles debut last time out 6 weeks ago and is likely to improve from that.

Bitofajokelike almost landed as a 125/1 shot when runner-up at Cork last time out over this distance. It's easy to see why the market respect is emphatic here in a serious drop in field quality after that impressive showing.

Slowly improving over hurdles and was a close up 4th at Leopardstown two starts ago running a lot better than odds of 100/1 might have suggested. Was let down by his jumping next time at Navan and had made several mistakes before coming to grief late on. Bounced back to form at Limerick last time when a close 3rd over 21f. Further improvement cannot be ruled out and hard to leave out of calculations and holds solid claims.

Tony Martin trained, and when the money appears, they normally do not leave it in the bookies' satchels. Second in a point-to-point, being his only run, which may see him improving on that run, with a big run on debut over hurdles.

Fortune The Brave was a bumper winner, but disappointed in two novice hurdles after. He steps up markedly in trip, which may help today. He has talent if he can start building on the recent runs. He showed fairly useful ability when winning over 2m 4f in bumpers, suggesting stamina is a strength. Up in distance today, but this significant step up in distance could suit him better as he is bred and shaped like a staying type.

Related to a couple of reasonable sorts, winners over hurdles, a chance is taken on Jonathan Sweeney trained Leading Light at a big price. One of just two newcomers in this maiden hurdle over 3m1f. By Gold Cup and St Leger winner Leading Light, pedigree suggests this lengthy trip will suit.

This modest chaser remains winless after 18 hurdle races. However, she achieved a commendable 5th place out of 12 in a handicap hurdle at Clonmel 3 months ago. Now facing a longer distance. The stables potential is uncertain, but the jockey brings a valuable 7lb claim. At odds of 66/1, this could be a smart each-way wager if the duo clicks.

Decent chaser and is 5lb below his chasing mark over hurdles even after winning on his latest hurdles outing. He only won by a head but was well ahead of the rest of the field. I think he can continue to improve and has every chance here of following up.

SPATMAN DE CERISY with his sound NH sire runs for a shrewd Irish yard who would not have too many handicap hurdlers rated as low as 90. This lightly-raced six year old has likely had this race as his off-season target given he was placed here last year and often well found in the market his chance looks at least as strong as others.

A highly competitive final handicap this evening, so therefore going each way. Terence O'Brien is a trainer who I admire, and he has Midnight Fairy here, who since handicapping has been a lot better, coming second both times. With the step up in trip, hopefully to bring more improvement, she can go close.

Rebellious Gale is back over hurdles on a very good mark, which can see him being a strong runner here for trainer Tony Martin and jockey Daniel King, getting his mount to hurdle with zest for a second win over hurdles.

Navy Waves has only won 1 of his 23 starts, and that was at Thurles back in November 22. He has, however, been placed in 3 of his last 4 starts. He was 2nd of 16 at Thurles in March and then third twice at Limerick and Clonmel last month. He is off the same mark but steps up from 2m1f at Clonmel to 3m1f here. He was 3rd at Kilbeggan over this distance last July, so looks like a good each-way bet with 5 places on offer.
This one is returning from a break as they are stepping it up in trip on its handicap debut with an interesting jockey booking/change. A good value each way bet for the 5 places available.

Running well last year, staying on strongly last time out in the closing stages, up half a furlong today. Jockey's had a couple of winners recently. Trainer had a couple finish in the money recently and looks set to go well once more here tonight.
Has won three times on the flat and has run okay in three hurdle races to date. Best of them being at Thurles, and a repeat of that effort would see this one make the frame.

This is very weak, and Nutbush should be on the premises. Finished runner-up latest to Willie Mullins' 2/5 on favorite, and that was only the second outing this year. Any improvement again can see a win here.

I'm not just picking this horse because I love the name CHOCOLATE TRUFFLES, but also because this mare is by Soldier of Fortune, and he is one of my favourite sires in relation to Irish jumps racing. His progeny are very effective on this going, and the trip shouldn't be a problem here. Worth a small punt each way.
A multiple winner on the flat and in good form the last twice over timber. Form of Limerick 3rd working out well with the winner going in again and the 2nd who I've tipped to win later on this card.

Onebrightbluerose has been running with credit on the last 3 runs and has every chance going into the final stages. Talented claimer takes the ride, adding to what already looks like a handy mark. Should threaten here again.
This looks wide open here, and with 5 places on offer and a claimer of 5 pounds, Navy Guitar becomes of interest at a big price. An improving 8th last time out and should be an EW chance here.
Scored at Sligo in October; ran wide and wasn't given a hard time when eleventh at Gowran next start. Worth a second look on this comeback.

Lightly raced under National Hunt rules. Tongue strap goes on for the first time, while Shadow Paddy goes handicapping over hurdles for the first time. Solid 5lb claimer on board. Stable's horses have been running pretty indifferently, but this one could go well.

BOLD BROOK is clear top-rated as a later-starting low-mileage type still likely with plenty more to offer through the handicap sphere. His qualifying efforts suggest he is well treated dropped 2lb from his handicap debut and given time since his last start he could be the answer.

PEBBLE TO A PEARL would have recieved a higher opening handicap mark had she finished closer to a couple of much higher rated types in her most recent qualifying run. She appeared to be capable of better and may well find her way over this trip in this sphere.
